design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing only - 'she wants to settle the August invoice today' - and the amount she must tender cannot be read off any record. It is the balance standing on the agreement, and that balance is wrong at the opening in three separate ways, none of which she mentions: the client discount for a kiosk trip the till never met has not been drawn, the product settlement for the period has never been raised on the invoice, and the credit the approved outage requests already owe has never been allowed. Each is a problem with its own multi-factor computation over the ledger, the service request log and the client's cafe contract at the same site; each must be discovered from the published rules alone, because the customer knows none of them. Difficulty is entirely in reading policy, reconciling history and getting four numbers exactly right in order - never in guessing which tool to use, and never in missing information: everything the agent needs is in the agreement, its 34 ledger rows, its 25 service requests, the cafe contract and its ledger, all reachable through the share finders.

SCOPE CLAIMED AND HEADROOM. Task 0 is the first task of this difficulty, so nothing was occupied before it. It claims market_ext_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown, market_ext_period_settlement_true_up, market_ext_outage_service_credit, market_ext_settlement_payment_amount and their four task tools post_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown_96ce656f, post_market_settlement_true_up_13e3670a, issue_market_outage_credit_49294a76, pay_market_settlement_invoice_693f0fba, occupying the subsidy drawdown, the product settlement true-up, the outage service credit and the settlement payment writes. Reserved for task 1 and untouched here: the subsidy funding lot write, the standby settlement raised while a market stands suspended, and the credit that hands back the unspent balance of a lapsed funding lot.

THE STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/tasks/micro_market_desk --task 0): {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5, 5]}. The tree has exactly three prerequisite problems besides the root; market_ext_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown took the count of 4 and the other three took 5 each.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: market_ext_settlement_payment_amount (the payment the customer asks for). Edges, all value_input:
  (a) market_ext_period_settlement_true_up <- market_ext_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown. gate: the window_subsidy binding. form: state. prerequisite sentence in market_ext_period_settlement_true_up's own rule: 'The settlement invoiced for a period is not worked out before the agreement's drawdown record carries the client discount owed for every kiosk trip the till failed to meet.' Four-point test: the ordering connective is 'not ... before'; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (what the agreement's drawdown record carries), not an action; no tool, policy id or code token appears; the strength is a hard requirement and the scope is exactly the trips the till failed to meet. Contrapositive: 'the settlement invoiced for a period is worked out only after the agreement's drawdown record carries the client discount owed for every kiosk trip the till failed to meet' - same result, same waited-on state, same scope. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: post_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown_96ce656f, the only write that books a subsidy drawdown. Derivation: the sentence says the drawdown record must carry the discount owed; the records show one service request naming a till transaction and still standing in the received state (initial_state.market_service_intake.ff917d14-4b20-42c9-b3be-c19997a906e8.related_reference = POS-40516903, request_status = received) and no drawdown posting carrying that till reference; market_ext_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown's own rule says what the catch-up drawdown books; so the one action is to book that drawdown. Resolving action owner: agent. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): with the drawdown, market_ext_period_settlement_true_up computes 400.11; skipping it, 398.58.
  (b) market_ext_outage_service_credit <- market_ext_period_settlement_true_up. gate: settlement_base. form: state. sentence in market_ext_outage_service_credit's own rule: 'The credit allowed for a settlement period is fixed only after the product settlement for that period stands charged on the agreement.' Connective 'only after'; record-visible state; no code token; hard strength. Exactly one write raises a product settlement charge: post_market_settlement_true_up_13e3670a (task 1's standby settlement raises the standing charge a market carries while it is shut, and its own rule says no product settlement is raised for such a period). Unresolved at the opening: the August invoice carries only its equipment line. Deletion sensitivity: 204.87 with, 158.35 without.
  (c) market_ext_settlement_payment_amount <- market_ext_period_settlement_true_up. gate: charges_side. form: state. sentence in market_ext_settlement_payment_amount's own rule: 'The amount tendered against a settlement invoice is not settled before the product settlement for that period stands charged on the agreement.' Deletion sensitivity: 704.86 with, 318.63 without.
  (d) market_ext_settlement_payment_amount <- market_ext_outage_service_credit. gate: credits_recent. form: state. sentence in market_ext_settlement_payment_amount's own rule: 'The amount tendered against a settlement invoice is not settled before a service credit carrying the kiosk whose lost hours it answers stands allowed against that invoice.' The state is record-visible because the two crediting tools of this difficulty write different rows: issue_market_outage_credit_49294a76 stamps the posting with the agreement's kiosk, and the lapsed-funding credit leaves the kiosk reference empty, which its own rule states. Exactly one write therefore produces a service credit carrying a kiosk. Unresolved at the opening: no service credit of any kind stands against INV-MK-440318, and the single credit on the agreement (45.00, 2026-09-02) sits against the already settled July invoice and carries an empty kiosk reference. Deletion sensitivity: 704.86 with, 806.13 without.
Topological order: market_ext_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown -> market_ext_period_settlement_true_up -> market_ext_outage_service_credit -> market_ext_settlement_payment_amount. The edges force a single total order, so there is no pair of writes that may be freely reordered and no second terminal state. user_scenario names none of the three prerequisite problems, the thing each resolves, or any hint toward them. The tool layer validates no prerequisite: each of the four functions performs one ctx.create and one ctx.update carrying that posting's own account delta, with no lookup of a preceding posting and no refusal path.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Step 8 writes market_subsidy_drawdown_posted, governed by market_subsidy_drawdown_rules (gate drawable_state: status active or suspended - active here) and by market_combination_dining_interaction, which carries no structured eligibility for that subject and is inherited as policy_scope; the pooled daily ceiling clause of that base policy is superseded by a declared overwrite on market_ext_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown. Step 10 writes market_monthly_settlement_invoiced, governed by market_settlement_terms (settlement_state: installing, active or suspended - active here), market_agg_portfolio_settlement_band and market_combination_dining_interaction (both policy_scope; the client holds one micro market, so the portfolio ladder sits on its lowest step, and base exempts a subsidy true-up from the band in any case). Step 12 writes market_service_credit_issued, governed by market_service_credit_terms, whose gate credit_claim_window is a time gate: anchor 'the day the settlement invoice was posted', anchor source market_ledger.posted_date, relation not_after, duration variants.service_credit_claim_window_days (21 for Standard Micro Market), calendar days counted from the day after the posting day, boundary inclusive. The August invoice line was posted 2026-09-10, so the window closes at the end of 2026-10-01; frozen_time is 2026-09-22, twelve days in. Boundary cases: a claim reaching the desk on 2026-10-01 is the last day still in time; on 2026-10-02 it is out of time and no credit may be allowed. Step 14 writes market_settlement_payment_posted, governed by market_settlement_payment_terms (payable_state: active, suspended or closed - active here). No base gate is retired by any overwrite on this task's writes; the declared overwrites replace amount bases, not gates.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The target object is the August settlement invoice INV-MK-440318 on micro market agreement 1543ba77-ecdf-4c37-8203-0db02b848006 at site CS-418, kiosk MK-44031. The correlation key for the credit and the payment is the invoice reference; for the drawdown it is the till transaction POS-40516903 named on the one service request that carries one. Rows excluded and why: the May shrink adjustment (initial_state.market_ledger.4ff9539e-81be-44df-8aa1-37db4a7b0228, posted 2026-06-14) falls outside the two-month shrink window; the June and July payments fall outside the two-month payment window; the largest drawdown ever posted (initial_state.market_ledger.f4cf186e-8b79-43b0-ba38-5498cfd4e3ab, 5.40 on 2025-09-10) sits outside every reading window and is the near-miss for the trip valuation factor; the 45.00 credit sits against the settled July invoice. Settlements already settled: the May, June and July invoices each carry a payment for their exact total (851.90, 868.60, 882.15), and the 45.00 credit allowed on 2026-09-02 leaves the client that much in credit on the July invoice, to be applied to the next settlement as base provides; the charges still standing are the August equipment line, the August shrink adjustment and the disputed May shrink adjustment, which is exactly receivable_balance_usd 1016.15.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The nineteen subsidy drawdown postings carry the trip valuation, the reading-window method and the fresh-cabinet share; every one of them is a single kiosk trip at or below the 5.50 daily ceiling printed against the format, and each carries the POS reference of the till transaction that drew it. The two funding lots fix the funding-depth step: only one falls inside the trailing year. The seven settlement charges and three payments carry the charge-reading window, the true-up share and the prompt-settlement discount. The two shrink adjustments and the two shrink disputes carry the withholding method. The twenty-five service requests carry the outage hours, their window, the declined-claim adjustment, the empty-market step and the cause share - and one of them, still in the received state, is the record of the kiosk trip the till failed to discount, which is deliberately not one of the approved outage hours. The cafe contract and its seven ledger rows carry the two cross-difficulty factors. Automatic clauses checked row by row: no invoice is past due beyond its grace days (the August invoice has eighteen days to run), the credit hold threshold of 75 days past due is nowhere near, the July suspension ran seven days and so falls below the format's minimum suspension of ten days and is handled as ordinary closed days with no standby charge, and no funding lot has reached its twelve-month expiry. No event-statistic cache is used, so no cache discrepancy is designed; both quantity fields reconcile exactly with the event stream at the opening and are maintained by every write.

PERSONA DESIGN. Marguerite is brisk and practical, talks in floors and buildings rather than references, and volunteers exactly three things: that she wants to settle the August invoice today, that she will run the payment herself by bank transfer, and the account code in front of her. Everything else comes only when asked. She cannot state the balance and says so, and she never corrects a figure. Her passive reactions hang on utterance events, never on the state of the database, and her last reaction answers the last gold action and stops there.

THE PREREQUISITE CHAIN, DEPTH AND BREADTH. The customer names the payment. The payment rule waits on two states: the product settlement standing charged for the period, and a service credit carrying the kiosk standing against the invoice. The settlement rule waits on the drawdown record carrying the discount owed for every trip the till failed to meet, and the credit rule waits on the same product settlement. Three hops from a bill to a missed kiosk discount. Breadth: the payment alone reads the settlement charges, the shrink adjustments, the credits, the payments, two shrink disputes, the invoice posting date, the payment history over a year and the client's cafe contract and cafe ledger. Remove any one of the four edges and a scored number changes (398.58, 158.35, 318.63, 806.13 against 400.11, 204.87, 704.86).

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Reading the trip value from the largest drawdown ever posted (5.40) rather than from the reading window. Taking the mean over the trailing quarter rather than the trailing year. Counting the outage hours over the quarter (8) instead of the half year (11), or forgetting that two claims were declined. Counting the received claim that names the missed trip as an approved outage hour - the rule says the hours are read from the requests approved on the agreement, and that one is not approved. Treating the period ceiling as binding - it is 352.45 against an allowed credit of 204.87. Setting the credits against the settlement in full instead of at the partial credit share. Adding the prompt-settlement discount and the group offset together instead of taking them one after the other.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate the profile by the organisation name, verify on the account code and the billing postcode, read the agreement, its ledger, its service request log, the cafe contract and the cafe ledger. Then: (1) book the catch-up drawdown of 2.75 for till transaction POS-40516903; (2) raise the August product settlement of 400.11 on INV-MK-440318; (3) allow the outage credit of 204.87 against the same invoice; (4) unlock the payment tool, hand it to the customer, and have her tender 704.86 by ach against INV-MK-440318.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The four computations were replayed against the seed with the real tools, each on the world as it stood at its own step: results 2.75, 400.11, 204.87 and 704.86, equal to computations[].expected and to the gold arguments. Per-factor baseline substitution moved the result in all nineteen cases; substituting every factor's baseline at once gave 3.05, 33.17, 70.49 and 60.49, each different from gold. Skipping each prerequisite write gave 398.58, 158.35, 318.63 and 806.13. Zeroing the history aggregates and forcing the cross-category reads off both moved every result. Every intermediate figure quoted in factor_trace and in argument_uniqueness_tracing was taken from a binding-by-binding dump of the same replay rather than written by hand.

user_scenario:
Marguerite Thornbury looks after workplace experience for Pinehurst Analytics Group out of their Chicago office, and the unattended micro market on the fourth floor there is hers to keep an eye on. She is ringing because the August micro market bill is still sitting open in her accounts payable queue and her finance director has told her to clear it before the quarter closes. She says so almost at once: she wants to settle the August invoice today, and she would rather run the payment herself from her own banking screen than have the desk move money on her behalf. She is happy for the desk to put the account straight first and says so plainly, but the money leaves on her instruction, by bank transfer out of their own payables run.

She is a brisk, friendly caller who talks in terms of floors and buildings rather than reference numbers. The account code printed on the invoice is CA-44207 and she reads it out early because it is the thing she has in front of her. If the agent needs another detail to be sure who it is, she reads the billing postcode off the top of the same invoice, 60614, and she will give her own direct line, 5035118427, if asked for something else again. She gives her name, Marguerite Thornbury, when she is asked who is calling. She has no idea what a kiosk reference or an agreement number is and says so; the most she can offer is that it is the market on the fourth floor at the Chicago office, and she leaves the agent to find it from that.

She cannot say what the invoice comes to. The portal shows it open, she says, but she has never trusted the number on that screen and would rather be told what the desk makes it. If the agent quotes her a figure she takes it at face value and does not argue with it. Asked whether there is a purchase order to quote, she says they put PO-PN-2026-118 on everything for that site this year. Asked how she wants to pay, she says bank transfer, the same way they always do.

If the agent tells her something else has to be put right on the account before the bill can be settled, she says that is fine and to carry on; she has no view on what it is, asks no questions about it, and does not press for detail. Whenever the agent tells her a charge or a discount has been put on the account, she says thank you and waits rather than volunteering anything further. She never offers a figure of her own and never tells the agent what the total ought to be.

Once the agent has unlocked the payment for her and told her the amount and the invoice it goes against, she runs it herself on the spot, by bank transfer, and reads back the confirmation she gets from her screen. When the desk tells her the payment is recorded against the invoice, she thanks them and rings off. She asks for nothing after that.
